messages:
alex.g: noticed odd tail spikes after enabling the continuous packer on the 13B fleet. small single-token requests sometimes see 150-250ms tails when they land in packs with long-running generations. wondering if packing is amplifying interference rather than smoothing it.

maria.t: can you paste a sample pack composition? are the short requests being merged with 1k+ token streams?

alex.g: yep, most of the offending packs look like [1x 5-token, 3x 1200-token] -> scheduler waited full pack window then fed all. log snippet: 
```
PACK_ID=0x7f3 | wait_ms=20 | requests=[r42(5t), r43(1240t), r44(980t)] | start_ts=1987654321000 | started_on=gpu-12
r42 latency=220ms (enqueue->first-token)
```

jordan.k: yikes. that's the classic packing latency amplification. two angles: prevent short ones from waiting behind long ones, or make long ones yield earlier (deadline propagation / preempt). i'm biased towards deadline-aware admission.

sam.p: or both. small fast requests should get a fastpath: if request.tokens < 32 && deadline < now+50ms then admit to fast queue that prefers immediate dispatch or tiny micro-packs. no full lane split, just a quick heuristic.

maria.t: micro-lanes are ok, but we must be careful about throughput regressions. fastpath must have strict cap to avoid starving long-running batches. also need to surface metrics so SRE can tune caps per hardware class.

jordan.k: agree on metrics. also consider pack trimming: when a long request is in-progress, if a short request arrives and the pack hasn't started execution, we could synthesize a tiny trimmed pack for the shorts and let the long run solo. cheap heuristic: if smallest_waiting_ms < threshold && fraction_long > 0.5 then split.

alex.g: love the trimmed-pack idea. it avoids hard lane semantics. we should also propagate per-request deadline to the runtime so device-side admission can preempt a queued request before kernel launch. that requires a small protocol: pack metadata carries per-request deadline and an ordered preempt bitmap.

sam.p: pseudo: 
```
if (request.deadline < pack.start + preempt_margin) {
  carve_out_short_pack(requests_with_tight_deadline)
} else {
  normal_pack()
}
```

maria.t: important: KV-cache warmups. long gens cause substantial KV churn; if we split packs we need to avoid thrashing the KV cache for tiny fast requests. maybe keep a tiny prefix-cache reserved for fastpath or bump warmup priority for short requests.

jordan.k: can we add a metric: pack_comp_short_frac, pack_kv_evictions_during_pack, per-pack-first-token-latency? if we collect 1 week of those we can pick thresholds.

alex.g: action items: 1) implement trimmed-pack heuristic prototype (sam+alex). 2) add pack composition + kv-eviction metrics (jordan). 3) run A/B on a small shard with fastpath cap=5% (maria + ops). i'll open an RFC follow-up with experiment plan.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/continuous-packer v2 -> staging at 2026-03-21T02:40Z :rocket:

maria.t: thanks — please include dashboard links in the RFC. small note: set default preempt_margin=10ms to start to avoid noisy preempts.

alex.g: will do, i'll also add an example of the pack metadata schema in the RFC.

jordan.k: cool. if trimmed-pack works we may avoid a full scheduler lane refactor.

sam.p: i'll start a tiny PR with the pseudo logic + unit tests.

alex.g: great, closing the thread for now. will ping when the PR lands. :thumbsup:
